siteSettings.tagline: Safe, supported homes for vulnerable people
siteSettings.heroTitle: A Home is More Than a House
siteSettings.heroSub: We provide safe, warm, supported homes where people can rebuild, belong and thrive — with dignity, choice and round-the-clock care when needed.

services.title: 24/7 Support
services.description: Waking nights and on-call help, so no one faces a crisis alone.
services.long: Our support workers provide consistent, respectful presence day and night, including sleep-in and waking night cover. We respond quickly and calmly, building trust over time.

services.title: Mental Health Support
services.description: Recovery-focused, trauma-informed coaching and wellbeing planning.
services.long: We work alongside NHS teams, using WRAP plans, coping strategies and gentle structure to help people stay well in their own home.

services.title: Life Skills Training
services.description: Cooking, budgeting, cleaning — practical skills for independent living.
services.long: Small steps, big wins. We teach in the kitchen, not the classroom, with visual recipes and patient coaching.

services.title: Community Integration
services.description: We connect people to work, learning, faith and friendship.
services.long: From football to pottery, we map local assets and support people to belong — not just be placed — in their neighbourhood.

services.title: Tenancy Sustainment
services.description: We help people keep their home when life gets tough.
services.long: Early help with benefits, arrears, neighbours and repairs. We advocate fiercely so tenancies don't fail.

services.title: Emergency Housing
services.description: Rapid, safe placements when crisis hits.
services.long: We hold a small number of emergency beds for social work referrals — safe tonight, with a plan for tomorrow.

news.title: Willow Cottage garden opens for neighbours
news.excerpt: Residents hosted a spring open day — 60 neighbours came, and the rhubarb sold out.
news.content: Last Saturday Willow Cottage opened its garden gates. With bunting made in art group, homemade cakes and tours of the new greenhouse, residents welcomed 60 local people. 'I was nervous at first,' said Sam, who lives at Willow, 'but everyone was so friendly. It feels like we really belong here now.' Proceeds from plant sales will fund a pizza oven. Our community team will now run monthly coffee mornings.
news.author: Maya P.

news.title: New PBS training for all support workers
news.excerpt: Positive Behaviour Support now embedded across every home — here's what changed.
news.content: We’ve invested in 3-day PBS training for all staff. Early results show fewer incidents and happier homes. Leila shares how low-arousal environments and active support make a difference.
news.author: David O.

news.title: Birch Court residents graduate college
news.excerpt: Three residents completed Level 2 Health & Social Care — with jobs to follow.
news.content: Huge congratulations to T, J and R at Birch Court who juggled tenancies, support sessions and college. All three have been offered bank support worker shifts with us.
news.author: Tom W.

news.title: Cost-of-living fund: £12k raised
news.excerpt: Local businesses donated to keep homes warm this winter.
news.content: Thanks to our partners at Bristol Energy Co-op, we raised £12k to top up prepayment meters and run warm spaces.
news.author: Fundraising Team

news.title: How we match people to homes
news.excerpt: It’s not first-come first-served — it’s about fit, safety and choice.
news.content: Our matching panel includes support workers, housing and — crucially — existing residents. We share anonymous profiles and visit together.
news.author: Jonah R.

news.title: Elmwood Lodge: sneak peek
news.excerpt: Sensory garden, ceiling hoists, wet rooms — a home built around complex needs.
news.content: Elmwood Lodge opens in June. Built with families, it includes a sensory room, adjustable kitchen and level-access garden.
news.author: Maya P.

faqs.question: Who can apply for a home?
faqs.answer: Adults 18+ who need support to live safely — learning disabilities, mental health, care leavers, homelessness risk, complex needs. We accept professional referrals and self-referrals.

faqs.question: How long does it take?
faqs.answer: Referral to viewing is typically 10-15 days. Matching depends on availability and fit. We keep you updated weekly.

faqs.question: Do you charge rent?
faqs.answer: Yes — rents are affordable and covered by Housing Benefit/UC housing costs in most cases. We help with benefit claims and have no hidden fees.

faqs.question: Can I bring my pet?
faqs.answer: In many homes, yes — case by case. Pets help wellbeing and we have a pet policy that supports responsible ownership.

faqs.question: What support hours do you provide?
faqs.answer: From a few floating hours to 24/7 including waking nights. Hours are agreed in your support plan and reviewed with you.

faqs.question: Do you work with social workers?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. We are CQC-regulated partners and attend MDTs, CPA reviews and safeguarding meetings. We share timely notes.

faqs.question: Are your homes regulated?
faqs.answer: We are a registered provider with Homes England, and our care is regulated by CQC. Latest reports on our About page.

faqs.question: Can I visit before deciding?
faqs.answer: Yes — we encourage daytime visits, overnight stays and meeting future housemates. No pressure, ever.
